title: Weapons to Russia, Wigs to China: How North Korea Balances Its Allies
author: Khang Vu
text:
Credit: ID 329431713 © Tomasragina | Dreamstime.com
North Korea’s balancing act is back in the spotlight. In September, it opened its first road bridge with Russia. Just last week, North Korea opened a similar one with China. Pyongyang’s land bridge with Russia will strengthen the bilateral arms trade while the one with China will provide it with energy products, raw materials, and heavy equipment for domestic consumption. The two bridges are a microcosm of how North Korea seeks to benefit from improved relations with Moscow and Beijing. North Korea is looking for military assistance from Russia and economic help from China. The clear division of labor ensures North Korea’s alliances with Russia and China are complementary, not competitive with each other.[...]
